name: motion-offered-nothing-moves
about: A first campaign on a connection with a video model, for a carrier whose enabled kinds of ad all show a thing at rest or a plain background. A motion ad is offered and nothing in any picture moves: the plan must be ready, and the recording shows whether the Strategist left the angles as stills.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Class A drivers who already pull flatbed and meet the experience the opening states, running or living near Midwest lanes. Many are likely out for long stretches or in a large fleet now. A clear pay per mile, weekly home time and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, stated plainly, with weekly home time beneath it.
angles.proof: The opening states a pay per mile and offers home weekly.
angles.why: Pay is the clearest fact of this job and a plain ground lets the rate carry the ad. No history yet, so nothing has been measured on hooks or formats; a plain ground gains nothing from motion.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, shown as arriving on the driver's own street at the end of a run.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Weekly home time is what separates regional work from longer runs. An arrival has movement, so motion is tried here; nothing has been measured about formats, so this is a test, not a known gain.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown parked with its flatbed, as the truck this driver keeps.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers care which truck they run, and assigned equipment is a concrete fact of this job. Nothing has been measured on formats; a parked truck gains nothing from motion, so still.

angles.idea: State plainly who this is for: Class A, flatbed, Midwest lanes, and the experience the opening asks for.
angles.proof: The job is Class A regional flatbed on Midwest lanes and states an experience requirement.
angles.why: With no lead history, stating the licence, lanes and experience up front should keep unqualified or out-of-area drivers from applying. Nothing measured on formats; a parked truck stays still.

angles.idea: Lead with the small fleet where dispatch knows your name, backed by the assigned truck and the retirement plan.
angles.proof: The carrier calls itself a small fleet where dispatch knows your name; the job lists an assigned truck and a retirement plan.
angles.why: The carrier's own words set it apart from large fleets, and listed facts keep the claim honest. Nothing has been measured for this carrier, formats included; a plain ground stays still.
